subject: Money
title: Bank Consolidation
description: A short lesson to help you apply Bank Consolidation.

hook.text: In 1985, the US had 14,000 banks. Today it has 4,200. Three out of four banks disappeared in 40 years.

buildup.text: Deregulation, technology, and mergers drove consolidation. Big banks absorbed small ones relentlessly.

discovery.text: The top 4 banks now hold 40% of all US deposits. Community banks shrink while mega-banks grow.

twist.text: Fewer banks means less competition. Customers have fewer choices and less power to negotiate rates and fees.

climax.text: Banking is becoming an oligopoly. A handful of institutions control the financial lives of 330 million people.

punchline.text: Fewer banks. Fewer choices. Higher fees.

quiz.question: How many US banks exist today compared to 1985?
